title: Practice 10: Perfective or imperfective? The prefixed verbs in use

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: He translated the Old Testament from Hebrew.
exercises.why: **перевёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **перевести** (to lead, to convey, to transfer, to move, to shift, to transmit, to switch) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **переводить**. past: он перевёл · она перевела́ · оно перевело́ · они перевели́. — Wiktionary, «перевести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **перевести**: to lead, to convey, to transfer, to move, to shift, to transmit, to switch; to translate, to interpret [with с (s, + genitive) ‘from a language’ and на (na, + accusative) ‘into a language’]; to remit (money).  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «переводить — перевести — to lead over; to transfer, to translate. Note the following meanings:.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choice: **переводил** is imperfective (**переводить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The situation drove Zoe to despair.
exercises.why: **довела** is the past tense (feminine) of **довести** (to lead, to take, to accompany (to), to bring (into); (cooking) to scald) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **доводить**. past: он довёл · она довела́ · оно довело́ · они довели́. — Wiktionary, «довести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **доводила** is imperfective (**доводить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Tom seems to have made off with the elk carcass.
exercises.why: **убежал** is the past tense (masculine) of **убежать** (to run away, to make off, to flee; to escape) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **убегать**. past: он убежа́л · она убежа́ла · оно убежа́ло · они убежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «убежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **убегал** is imperfective (**убегать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: A person named Williams came to see you yesterday.
exercises.why: **приходил** is the past tense (masculine) of **приходить** (to come (to), to arrive (at) (place, conclusion, state of abandonment, anger, insanity)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **прийти**. past: он приходи́л · она приходи́ла · оно приходи́ло · они приходи́ли. — Wiktionary, «приходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто это идёт (едет) сюда?» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **пришёл** is perfective (**прийти**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **привёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **привести** (to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приводить**. past: он привёл · она привела́ · оно привело́ · они привели́. — Wiktionary, «привести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **приводил** is imperfective (**приводить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Tom carried two boxes into the storage room.
exercises.why: **отнёс** is the past tense (masculine) of **отнести** (to carry, to deliver; (of wind) to carry (off, away), to sweep (away)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **относить**. past: он отнёс · она отнесла́ · оно отнесло́ · они отнесли́. — Wiktionary, «отнести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Compare: «Я отнёс письмо на почту.» (I took (on foot) the letter to the post office.) — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choice: **относил** is imperfective (**относить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The priceless china shattered into fragments.
exercises.why: **разлетелся** is the past tense (masculine) of **разлететься** (to fly away, to scatter (in the air); to come apart, to be blown apart) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **разлетаться**. past: он разлете́лся · она разлете́лась · оно разлете́лось · они разлете́лись. — Wiktionary, «разлететься» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. Antonym: с-, со- (+сь, +ся) Example: Дед Мороз разнёс подарки по домам. — Grandfather Frost brought the gifts to the (various) houses. После ужина, мы разошлись по домам. — After dinner, we went to our separate homes. Prepositional phrases: по + dat. pl.; в + acc. pl.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **разлетался** is imperfective (**разлетаться**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **подошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **подойти** (to approach, to come to, to walk to, to draw near [with к (k)]; to fit, to suit, to match, to be right [with dative]) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **подходить**. past: он подошёл · она подошла́ · оно подошло́ · они подошли́. — Wiktionary, «подойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**под-, подо-** — Approach. Antonym: от- Example: Он подошёл к девушке, чтобы спросить её номер. — He approached the girl to ask for her number. Prepositional phrases: к + dat.; до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **подходил** is imperfective (**подходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The liner called at Hong Kong.
exercises.why: **зашёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **зайти** (to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; to pick up, to fetch) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **заходить**. past: он зашёл · она зашла́ · оно зашло́ · они зашли́. — Wiktionary, «зайти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **заходил** is imperfective (**заходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Black clouds were passing above the city.
exercises.why: **проплывали** is the past tense (plural) of **проплывать** (to swim by, to float by, to sail by; to swim (a certain distance or time), to sail (a certain distance or time)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **проплыть**. past: он проплыва́л · она проплыва́ла · оно проплыва́ло · они проплыва́ли. — Wiktionary, «проплывать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **проплыли** is perfective (**проплыть**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: We spent the entire day in Yoyogi Park.
exercises.why: **провели** is the past tense (plural) of **провести** (to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take; to lay, to construct, to build, to install a road, a pipe, a wire etc.) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проводить**. past: он провёл · она провела́ · оно провело́ · они провели́. — Wiktionary, «провести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Compare: «Я хорошо провёл время.» (I had a good time.) — DLI, Lesson 79. «Мы провели в Европе два месяца.» (We spent two months in Europe.) — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choice: **проводили** is imperfective (**проводить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: It took many years to build it.
exercises.why: **ушло** is the past tense (neuter) of **уйти** (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уходить**. past: он ушёл · она ушла́ · оно ушло́ · они ушли́. — Wiktionary, «уйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **уходило** is imperfective (**уходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **отлетела** is the past tense (feminine) of **отлететь** (to fly away, to fly off; to rebound, to bounce back) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **отлетать**. past: он отлете́л · она отлете́ла · оно отлете́ло · они отлете́ли. — Wiktionary, «отлететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. exercises.q: This is the Volga. We crossed it on a motorboat.
exercises.why: **переплыли** is the past tense (plural) of **переплыть** (to swim across; to sail across) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **переплывать**. past: он переплы́л · она переплыла́ · оно переплы́ло · они переплы́ли. — Wiktionary, «переплыть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. The other choice: **переплывали** is imperfective (**переплывать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **подошли** is the past tense (plural) of **подойти** (to approach, to come to, to walk to, to draw near [with к (k)]; to fit, to suit, to match, to be right [with dative]) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **подходить**. past: он подошёл · она подошла́ · оно подошло́ · они подошли́. — Wiktionary, «подойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**под-, подо-** — Approach. exercises.q: The butterfly fluttered from flower to flower.
exercises.why: **перелетала** is the past tense (feminine) of **перелетать** (to fly (from one place to another or above something); to fly too far, to overshoot (the mark)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **перелететь**. past: он перелета́л · она перелета́ла · оно перелета́ло · они перелета́ли. — Wiktionary, «перелетать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Compare: «Линдберг перелетел через Атлантический океан.» (Perfective, past) — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choice: **перелетела** is perfective (**перелететь**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
